text:
Asha: FYI customer 'acme-337' opened a ticket: large batch job triggering 429s and "quota exceeded" errors around 09:12 UTC. They reported the payloads were primarily /v1/generate calls.
Mike: Can you paste the exact error payload + response headers? need to know if it's per-key or per-customer aggregation.
Asha: They included: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","detail":"burst_exhausted"}` and headers: `x-rate-limit-limit: 15000`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 78`, `x-retry-after: 25`.
Sylvie: remaining=0 + retry-after present = definitely quota-layer throttle. Could still be either per-key burst or global sustained. Do we have model/route?
Asha: route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3b-quant. Most requests were non-streaming.
Kai: Quick checklist for triage:
- Check per-customer burst tokens and sustained minute-window in Quotas dashboard.
- Inspect Throttles dashboard (group by customer_id, route, model, reason).
- Pull infra logs for contiguous window to see sequence of outcomes (accept vs throttled).
Jorge: Logs snippet I pulled: 
``` 
2026-03-14T09:11:50Z INFO req=aa111 cust=acme-337 route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3b-quant tokens=768 outcome=accept
2026-03-14T09:11:52Z WARN req=bb222 cust=acme-337 route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3b-quant tokens=768 outcome=throttled reason=burst_quota_exhausted
2026-03-14T09:11:55Z WARN req=cc333 cust=acme-337 route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3b-quant tokens=1024 outcome=throttled reason=sustained_quota_exhausted
2026-03-14T09:12:30Z INFO req=dd444 cust=acme-337 route=/v1/generate model=rwd-3b-quant tokens=256 outcome=accept
``` 
Jorge: pattern = quick burst, then flip to sustained throttle.
Priya: Did they change client behavior recently? We see a lot of these from new batch jobs that fan out lots of parallel workers with no backoff.
Asha: They admitted they rolled a job that started 200 concurrent processes hitting the API at once. No retry backoff configured.
Mike: That explains it. Reminder of our quota hierarchy: small burst bucket that refills quickly plus a per-minute sustained allowance. Large instantaneous concurrency will exhaust burst bucket and then you hit sustained throttles.
Sylvie: Observability suggestions to hand to support: include these dashboard panels in the share:
- throttled_requests_by_customer (stacked by reason)
- throttle_rate_pct (throttled/total over 1m and 5m)
- per-route concurrency heatmap (concurrent requests per route per-minute)
- model_token_burn_per_minute (tokens/min by model)
- recent_traces_with_last_throttle_reason tag
Also suggest adding a table view: top 10 customers by throttle_count last 24h.
Kai: For immediate support playbook: 1) provide them a repro curl to reproduce safely (small concurrency) 2) share dash links and one-line explanation 3) offer 1-hour uplift to burst tokens or suggest staggering.
Asha: Repro we gave (conservative):
```bash
# run 20 concurrency to mimic but not break things
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -X POST "$API_HOST/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "x-customer-id: acme-337" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-quant","input":"smoke test","max_tokens":256}' &
done; wait
```
Asha: Also recommended client changes: cap concurrency to 20, implement exponential backoff with jitter (initial 100ms, cap 10s), and switch to streaming where possible to reduce peak token burn.
Jorge: I ran a DB query to attribute throttles: 
```
SELECT reason, count(*) as cnt, route, model
FROM request_events
WHERE customer_id='acme-337' AND ts > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY reason, route, model
ORDER BY cnt DESC
```
Jorge: Results: burst_quota_exhausted=4200, sustained_quota_exhausted=1150. So most are burst.
Priya: Also check if multiple API keys are active under the same account (aggregated against customer quota).
Mike: Good call. Asha, flag billing -> API keys activity and confirm only one key is being used.
Asha: They confirmed 1 key but many k8s pods sharing it.
Sylvie: Platform action items we should take after fixing customer:
- Create an alert: when throttle_rate_by_customer > 3% for 15m, page support-oncall with context {customer_id, top_route, top_model, dominant_reason}.
- Add per-minute waterfall panel separating burst vs sustained reasons.
- Add route+model labels to 429 logs and include `throttle_reason` in 429 response body for actionable client behavior (small RFC).
Kai: Also add a Grafana drilldown link from alert to the customer usage timeseries and a query that pre-populates customer_id and timeframe. Makes support quicker.
Mike: For remediation options to propose to customer: a) temporary +2x burst for 1 hour (manual), b) instruct to spread the workload or use a queuing layer, c) switch to a cheaper model for batch jobs, d) enable streaming where applicable.
Asha: I granted a 1-hour temporary burst uplift and asked them to retry with lower concurrency. They reported retries dropped to <1% errors.
Priya: Please note final root cause = 200-concurrency sudden fan-out consuming burst tokens, followed by sustained-rate throttles; mitigation = burst uplift + client backoff + reduce concurrency.
Jorge: I'll add a dashboard tile to the runbook (throttles -> per-customer heatmap) and add an annotation on the spike minute linking to this ticket.
OncallBot: Incident note created: INC-2026-4521 (customer throttle spike) assigned to eng-sre. Link: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-4521
Sylvie: Filing a small engineering RFC to add `throttle_reason` and `recommended_wait` to 429 payload so clients get more actionable info. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform.
Mike: Also surface this in support KB: "How to interpret 429s and next steps" with checklist and recommended dashboard tiles.
Asha: Closing loop with customer and updating the ticket with the repro, mitigation steps, and links to dashboards. Thanks everyone :pray:
